routing_warnings.description: The message changes the hero headline rather than the main-page architecture.
The message asks about the Request Early Access button behavior rather than the main-page architecture.
The message defines navigation from the Request Early Access button to the contact-form page.
The message supplies contact-page copy rather than changing the main landing-page architecture.
The message concerns replacement of the hero product image.
The reported typo is on the contact page and does not establish a failure of the main-page architecture.
The message changes where the landing website is hosted, not its page architecture.
The request concerns depicting the hero photo inside a mobile-phone visual, not responsive layout behavior.
The message concerns replacing the hero graphic with an image depicting the sales page on a phone, not verifying or changing mobile responsiveness.
The launch-video and LOTCLIP hero-asset clauses concern the independently defined hero product visualization rather than the overall visual design style.
The client selects one of the hero-section options, which is more narrowly associated with the hero product visualization.
The requested hero-image replacement is separate from the same message’s approval of the overall design.
The requested founder-image replacement belongs to the independently defined bottom-of-page image Requirement.
The instruction limiting the dealer-login button to the top-right corner belongs to the Dealer Login CTA Requirement.
The unresolved reference to an image not yet being added follows the hero-image discussion and does not clearly entail the bottom-of-page image.
The reported launch failure concerns displacement of the existing product's root-domain routing, not the choice of Webflow or its site plan.
The proposed subdomain changes the landing site's DNS destination rather than its Webflow platform or plan.
The proposed URL concerns selection of a landing-page subdomain.
The client supplies the specific landing-page subdomain rather than changing the Webflow platform or plan.
Removing the Webflow DNS record is a remediation step for restoring the product root domain.
The message verifies restoration of the existing product's root-domain routing.
The same message reports a distinct Firebase Hosting failure for the product's www hostname.
The reported launch failure concerns displacement of the existing product at the root domain, not execution of the later-selected landing-site subdomain.
The client requests restoration of the previous root-domain record.
The client asks whether the previous root-domain destination can be restored.
The message concretely verifies restoration of the product's root-domain routing.
The remaining Site Not Found failure and Firebase remediation instructions concern the separate www hostname.
The client directs that the Webflow sales website be hosted on a subdomain; this changes the landing-site routing Requirement rather than the product root-domain Requirement.
The remaining Firebase Hosting failure and Site Not Found behavior for [URL_026] belong to the separate product www-domain routing Requirement.
The opening clause independently verifies that the root-domain product site is online and serving normally; that observation belongs to the root-domain routing Requirement.
